tour.name: Lake Titicaca Private Boat Tour from Puno: Uros Floating Islands & Taquile
tour.subtitle: A private day on the highest navigable lake in the world with a licensed guide and boat: the floating reed islands of the Uros people, a crossing of the deep-blue lake, and the island of Taquile, whose men knit and whose textile art is recognised by UNESCO, with lunch of fresh trout.

highlights: Lake Titicaca at 3,812 metres, between Peru and Bolivia
The floating islands of the Uros, built of totora reeds
A ride in a traditional reed boat
The island of Taquile, its stone arches and terraces
Taquile's textile art, recognised by UNESCO
Lunch of fresh lake trout with a view
A private boat and licensed guide
tour.overview:
Lake Titicaca, at 3,812 metres in the Andes, is the largest lake in South America and is often called the highest navigable lake in the world. In Andean belief it is the birthplace of the sun and of Manco Cápac, the first Inca. The Uros people live on dozens of islands they build themselves from layers of totora reeds, which they must constantly renew; on the island of Taquile, Quechua families maintain a communal way of life and a weaving tradition – practised by the men as well as the women – inscribed as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2008.

This private day takes you on your own boat with a licensed guide, from the port of Puno to the Uros islands and on to Taquile.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Puno
• Type: private boat with licensed guide
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; a walk of about 2 hours with climbs on Taquile, at 3,800 to 4,000 metres

WHAT YOU SEE
• The bay of Puno.
• The Uros floating islands.
• The open waters of the lake.
• Taquile island.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private boat avoids the crowded group launches and lets you choose a quieter Uros island and the time you spend on each.

WHO IT SUITS
Culture lovers, photographers and families.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you have more time, a homestay night on Amantaní island is unforgettable.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The sun is very strong at this altitude, and the wind on the lake is cold: bring sun protection and warm layers. Puno is a long journey from Cusco, by the scenic train, bus or a flight to Juliaca.

days.name: The Uros floating islands, a reed boat ride, Taquile island and a trout lunch
days.description:
What to expect: the people and landscapes of Lake Titicaca from a private boat, with a licensed guide, fees and lunch.

Your guide collects you at your hotel at about 7:00 and takes you to the port of Puno, where your private boat is waiting. You cross the bay, through channels in the reed beds, to the Uros islands, about 30 minutes away. On one of the islands, the families welcome you and show you how they cut blocks of totora root, tie them together and pile layers of reeds on top to make the floor, which they renew every few weeks as the bottom rots away, and how they build their houses, boats and watchtowers from the same reed. You walk on the springy surface, learn a few words of Aymara or Uro, and ride across the channel in a reed boat with a puma's head on its prow.

Your boat then crosses the open lake, about two hours, towards Taquile, with the mountains of Bolivia on the horizon on clear days. You land and walk up through terraced fields and stone arches to the main square, where the community's textiles are displayed. Your guide explains how the islanders' clothing shows their status: married men wear red knitted caps, single men caps with white tips, and the men knit constantly as they walk; the women weave the colourful belts. Lunch is fresh trout from the lake, with quinoa soup, on a terrace overlooking the water. You walk down to the other side of the island to rejoin the boat and return to Puno, arriving at about 16:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
07:30 – Boat to the Uros islands.
08:00 – Uros islands and reed boat ride.
09:30 – Crossing to Taquile.
11:30 – Taquile: walk, main square and textiles.
13:00 – Trout lunch.
14:00 – Boat back to Puno.
16:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A homestay on Amantaní or Taquile can be added for a night.
• The Sillustani funerary towers make a good afternoon on another day.
• Bring small change to buy crafts directly from the islanders.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the boat private?
faq.answer: Yes, your own boat and crew with your licensed guide.

faq.question: Are the fees and lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes: the Uros and Taquile entrance fees, the reed boat ride and a trout lunch.

faq.question: Are the floating islands touristy?
faq.answer: Some are. With a private boat we visit a quieter family island, and your guide explains the real life of the Uros today.

faq.question: Is the altitude a problem?
faq.answer: Puno and the lake are at about 3,800 metres; Taquile involves climbing. Acclimatise in Cusco first and take it slowly.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the floating islands and the reed boats. Life jackets are provided.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The Uros islands are easy but soft underfoot; Taquile requires a steep walk.

faq.question: Can we stay overnight on the lake?
faq.answer: Yes. A homestay with a family on Amantaní or Taquile is a wonderful experience.

faq.question: How do we get to Puno?
faq.answer: By the scenic Titicaca train or a tourist bus from Cusco, about 10 hours, or a flight to Juliaca airport, an hour from Puno.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Peru but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Warm layers, a windproof jacket, a hat, sunglasses and strong sun cream.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: May to October is dry and sunny but cold at night. Early February brings the colourful Candelaria festival in Puno.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
